thought_text: Meeting with the public is always a unique experience.
Nothing like people paid to keep asking you for favors.

Europe's cheese and wine on our shelves?

Fish don't know about borders. So how do we make this work?

Plenty of people in this chamber got where they are through a friend of a friend.
One wage across three regions. Living costs do not match across them.
Members drawing their own district lines is a bit like a referee picking the teams.

Long-term residents pay taxes and send their kids to school here. The ballot is another matter.
Some land is worth more standing than cut.
A town without a hospital slowly stops being a town.
Convenience is never free. Someone always holds the keys.
A free voice is only as strong as the hand that funds it.
Sunlight is a fine disinfectant, but it burns too.
Every tax cut is a promise someone else pays for.
People will pay for a clean sky if they trust where the money goes.
The sea keeps a ledger, and it is running short.
A fleet is a promise. Someone must keep the yards alive to keep it.
A constitution that never changes dies. One that changes carelessly dies faster.
Open doors speed trade, but someone must still watch the door.
Wealth on a contested shore comes with a bill nobody prints.
Trade is friendship with a price tag. Read it carefully.
A field without a farmer is only land.
Knowledge is the only crop that grows in every season.
Fairness at work is not a favor. It is a floor.

Safety and freedom both die in the same dark corner.
A village is more than its budget line.
A leader chosen in the dark answers to the dark.
Fares and timetables decide whether people can live where they work.

Listening costs nothing and teaches everything.

Helping the party on farm policy helps real farms, too.

Artisans ask for respect before they ask for money.

The people who gain are Ainu families and language teachers. The people who pay are town budgets and landholders.
My worry is disputes over ancestral land claims. My hope is that Ainu families and language teachers come out better off.
The people who gain are rice and dairy farmers. The people who pay are taxpayers and grocery shoppers.
My worry is overproduction paid for by the treasury. My hope is that rice and dairy farmers come out better off.
The people who gain are new employers and the workers they hire. The people who pay are workers under looser labor rules.
My worry is a race to the bottom on labor protections. My hope is that new employers and the workers they hire come out better off.
The people who gain are commuters, freight shippers and tourist towns. The people who pay are the national budget.
My worry is cost overruns on tunnels and track. My hope is that commuters, freight shippers and tourist towns come out better off.
The people who gain are island residents and coast guard crews. The people who pay are the defense budget.
My worry is escalating tension with Russia. My hope is that island residents and coast guard crews come out better off.
The people who gain are employers short of workers. The people who pay are wage levels and local services.
My worry is exploitation of workers and strained housing. My hope is that employers short of workers come out better off.
The people who gain are rural towns and households that lost power. The people who pay are utility customers and the budget.
My worry is projects delayed by local objections. My hope is that rural towns and households that lost power come out better off.
The people who gain are pensioners and elder care. The people who pay are shoppers and small shops.
My worry is weaker spending in poorer households. My hope is that pensioners and elder care come out better off.
The people who gain are prefectural governments and local officials. The people who pay are poorer areas that depend on transfers.
My worry is gaps between rich and poor prefectures. My hope is that prefectural governments and local officials come out better off.
The people who gain are women candidates and their voters. The people who pay are party selection committees.
My worry is qualified candidates passed over. My hope is that women candidates and their voters come out better off.
The people who gain are ferry operators, fishers and border towns. The people who pay are the foreign affairs budget.
My worry is a commission with no power to settle anything. My hope is that ferry operators, fishers and border towns come out better off.
The people who gain are courts that want distance from politics. The people who pay are the Cabinet's control over nominations.
My worry is an unelected body choosing judges. My hope is that courts that want distance from politics come out better off.
The people who gain are temples, shrines and festival towns. The people who pay are the treasury and secular taxpayers.
My worry is favoring some faiths over others. My hope is that temples, shrines and festival towns come out better off.
The people who gain are districts with a member who can deliver. The people who pay are the national budget.
My worry is pork spending that buys votes. My hope is that districts with a member who can deliver come out better off.
The people who gain are tech firms and graduates. The people who pay are tax revenue and local power supply.
My worry is subsidies for firms that would come anyway. My hope is that tech firms and graduates come out better off.
The people who gain are police and crime victims. The people who pay are privacy and free speech.
My worry is wiretaps used against ordinary protest. My hope is that police and crime victims come out better off.
The people who gain are same-sex couples and their families. The people who pay are traditional family norms in some eyes.
My worry is a split in public opinion. My hope is that same-sex couples and their families come out better off.
The people who gain are emergency responders after a disaster. The people who pay are checks and balances.
My worry is power kept longer than the crisis lasts. My hope is that emergency responders after a disaster come out better off.
The people who gain are defense planners and allies. The people who pay are neutral foreign policy.
My worry is being drawn into a foreign conflict. My hope is that defense planners and allies come out better off.
The people who gain are exporters and shoppers. The people who pay are dairy and rural producers.
My worry is foreign dairy undercutting local farms. My hope is that exporters and shoppers come out better off.
The people who gain are coastal communities and security officials. The people who pay are foreign investors and sellers.
My worry is scaring off honest investment. My hope is that coastal communities and security officials come out better off.
The people who gain are hotels, shops and artisans. The people who pay are border officials and crowded sites.
My worry is overcrowded resorts and strained services. My hope is that hotels, shops and artisans come out better off.
The people who gain are fishers and island tour operators. The people who pay are our claim to the islands.
My worry is weakening our claim to the islands. My hope is that fishers and island tour operators come out better off.
The people who gain are power users and industry. The people who pay are nearby fishers and communities.
My worry is an accident after a quake. My hope is that power users and industry come out better off.
The people who gain are construction workers, hotels and the host town. The people who pay are neighbors and gambling-prone households.
My worry is gambling addiction and organized crime. My hope is that construction workers, hotels and the host town come out better off.
The people who gain are applicants without connections. The people who pay are members who place their supporters.
My worry is exams that miss real-world skill. My hope is that applicants without connections come out better off.
The people who gain are low-wage workers and students. The people who pay are small shops and farms.
My worry is closed shops and fewer jobs in poor towns. My hope is that low-wage workers and students come out better off.
The people who gain are voters in unfairly drawn districts. The people who pay are members who benefit from today's lines.
My worry is an unelected commission with too much say. My hope is that voters in unfairly drawn districts come out better off.
The people who gain are schools and families who want a shared moral base. The people who pay are students and teachers with other views.
My worry is the state teaching one view of virtue. My hope is that schools and families who want a shared moral base come out better off.
The people who gain are foreign residents and their neighbors. The people who pay are the idea that voting belongs to citizens.
My worry is a backlash that harms community ties. My hope is that foreign residents and their neighbors come out better off.
The people who gain are wildlife, Ainu land users and tourism. The people who pay are loggers and developers.
My worry is lost jobs in forest towns. My hope is that wildlife, Ainu land users and tourism come out better off.
The people who gain are rural patients. The people who pay are the health budget.
My worry is small hospitals with too few doctors. My hope is that rural patients come out better off.
The people who gain are residents who tire of paperwork. The people who pay are privacy.
My worry is a data breach exposing everyone's records. My hope is that residents who tire of paperwork come out better off.
The people who gain are viewers who want independent news. The people who pay are government control of messaging.
My worry is a broadcaster answerable to no one. My hope is that viewers who want independent news come out better off.
The people who gain are voters who want clean politics. The people who pay are parties and members who rely on big donors.
My worry is money moving to groups outside the rules. My hope is that voters who want clean politics come out better off.
The people who gain are firms and their shareholders. The people who pay are tax revenue for services.
My worry is cuts to services to pay for the tax cut. My hope is that firms and their shareholders come out better off.
The people who gain are clean-energy firms and households that get dividends. The people who pay are fuel users, farmers and fishers.
My worry is higher costs in cold, spread-out towns. My hope is that clean-energy firms and households that get dividends come out better off.
The people who gain are fishers and consumers who want healthy stocks. The people who pay are small buyers and boats that sell quotas.
My worry is quotas concentrated in a few large boats. My hope is that fishers and consumers who want healthy stocks come out better off.
The people who gain are shipyard workers and defense suppliers. The people who pay are other spending and taxpayers.
My worry is waste on a closed circle of contractors. My hope is that shipyard workers and defense suppliers come out better off.
The people who gain are members who want change studied. The people who pay are time and attention in the Assembly.
My worry is a commission that pushes a hidden agenda. My hope is that members who want change studied come out better off.
The people who gain are traders and travelers. The people who pay are privacy and some border jobs.
My worry is data shared without limits. My hope is that traders and travelers come out better off.
The people who gain are investors and some island jobs. The people who pay are fishers, the sea and island heritage.
My worry is damage to fisheries and sacred sites. My hope is that investors and some island jobs come out better off.
The people who gain are exporters and shoppers. The people who pay are workers and producers who compete with imports.
My worry is dependence on one big trading partner. My hope is that exporters and shoppers come out better off.
The people who gain are young farmers and farm towns. The people who pay are the treasury.
My worry is grants for farms that cannot survive. My hope is that young farmers and farm towns come out better off.
The people who gain are researchers and students. The people who pay are the national budget.
My worry is funds spent on the wrong things. My hope is that researchers and students come out better off.
The people who gain are women, minorities and disabled workers. The people who pay are employers who must change hiring.
My worry is red tape and disputes at small firms. My hope is that women, minorities and disabled workers come out better off.
The people who gain are working parents and children. The people who pay are employers and the budget.
My worry is staff shortages at small firms. My hope is that working parents and children come out better off.
The people who gain are police and commuters. The people who pay are privacy.
My worry is tracking innocent people. My hope is that police and commuters come out better off.
The people who gain are taxpayers and bigger towns. The people who pay are small towns' identity and local jobs.
My worry is far-away offices and lost local voices. My hope is that taxpayers and bigger towns come out better off.
The people who gain are rank-and-file members. The people who pay are party elders and the members' influence.
My worry is leaders chosen by loud, small factions. My hope is that rank-and-file members come out better off.
